title: Why Staying at One Company Costs You 50% in Income

beats.say: Staying at the same job for over 2 years costs you 50% in lifetime earnings.
beats.visual: Low angle silhouette of a lone worker walking past massive cold concrete office pillars in heavy driving rain.

beats.say: You're taught that staying loyal pays off through bigger promotions and steady annual pay raises.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of a cheap corporate ID badge resting on wet asphalt under cold fluorescent light.

beats.say: Why does company loyalty cap your paycheck while job switching multiplies your income?
beats.visual: High angle wide shot of an empty glass elevator ascending a dark skyscraper during blue hour.

beats.say: Most workers assume staying put and working hard guarantees the highest long-term salary growth.
beats.visual: Fog cutting through a towering city office skyline illuminated by sodium streetlights at midnight.

beats.say: In reality, internal raises average just 3%, which that's barely keeping pace with 3% inflation.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of hands typing on a glowing laptop keyboard in a pitch-black room.

beats.say: So how's that tiny 3% raise compounding into a massive 50% lifetime earnings loss?
beats.visual: Wide angle shot of a solitary person standing at the edge of a dark rain-slicked highway underpass.

beats.say: When you switch companies, average job-hop raises jump between 10% and 20% instantly.
beats.visual: Low angle shot looking up at towering corporate steel beams framed by thick fog and cold light.

beats.say: But why do corporate payroll budgets aggressively favor outside hires over their most loyal workers?
beats.visual: Silhouette of a commuter standing alone on an empty train platform during a midnight downpour.

beats.say: Retention budgets are anchored to your starting salary, strictly capped by rigid corporate policy.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of a heavy steel vault door locking under a single harsh spotlight.

beats.say: Meanwhile, competitive hiring budgets must match current market rates just to pull in new talent.
beats.visual: High angle view of wet city street reflecting harsh neon store lights in the dark.

beats.say: Company loyalty caps your paycheck because internal raises stay at 3% while hiring budgets pay market rates.
beats.visual: Extreme wide shot of a giant illuminated office tower rising into dark storm clouds.

beats.say: Reframe your labor as a business service rather than an emotional family loyalty.
beats.visual: Low angle silhouette of a person looking out from a high-floor office glass window over a sprawling city.

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you, so staying quiet never costs you fortune.
beats.visual: Rain-slicked city avenue reflecting red taillights fading into the midnight horizon.

caption: Company loyalty is draining your long-term wealth. Here is the math behind job switching. #money #careers #personalfinance #salary #quietmoney
description: Staying at one company longer than two years can cost you up to 50% in lifetime earnings. Learn why corporate budgets cap internal raises at 3% while paying market rates for new hires.
first_comment: How long have you been at your current job?

facts.claim: Staying at a company over two years costs 50% in lifetime earnings on average.
facts.basis: Forbes analysis on workforce salary data by Cameron Keng.

facts.claim: Internal salary raises average ~3% while job switching yields 10% to 20% increases.
facts.basis: ADP Pay Insights workforce data on job-stayers vs. job-switchers.

loop_map.stakes: Staying at the same job for over 2 years costs you 50% in lifetime earnings.
loop_map.big_question: Why does company loyalty cap your paycheck while job switching multiplies your income?
loop_map.assume: Staying loyal and working hard brings the highest long-term salary growth.
loop_map.reveal: Internal raises average 3% while job switching yields 10% to 20% increases due to market-rate anchoring.
